headline: Two more Nevada House seats called for Democrats; Senate count unchanged
body: The Associated Press has called two more House races in Nevada, according to the Guardian's live results tracker, which carries AP race calls. Democratic Rep. Dina Titus wins Nevada's 1st District, 60.3% to 37.2% over Republican Carrie Buck with about 65% of the expected vote counted. Democratic Rep. Susie Lee wins Nevada's 3rd District, 60.1% to 37.8% over Republican Marty O'Donnell with about 65% counted. Neither seat changed party. The tracker now shows 360 House races called, 222 for Democrats and 138 for Republicans, with 25 House seats called for a different party than before. The Senate count is unchanged at 33 races called, 20 for Democrats and 13 for Republicans, with Mississippi and Alaska still uncalled. In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom leads Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 43 votes with about 96% of the expected vote counted, and in Alaska, Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan leads Democrat Mary Peltola by about 1,700 votes with about 69% counted. These are vote counts and AP race calls, not certified results, and counting continues.

headline: First race calls: Democrats hold Virginia's Senate seat; early House calls in Kentucky and Florida
body: With the first polls closed across the East, the first race calls of the night have come in. The Guardian's live results tracker, which shows Associated Press race calls, has Democrats holding the Senate seat in Virginia. In the House, it shows Democrats holding Kentucky's 3rd district and Florida's 10th, and Republicans holding Kentucky's 5th. These are media projections, not official results; state counts continue and certification comes weeks later. Neither chamber has been called. AP says control of the Senate could take days to settle and the House up to about a week, with ranked-choice tabulation possible in Alaska and Maine. Democrats need to flip four Senate seats and three House seats to win control, according to AP.
